subject: End-to-end latency requirements: hosted vs incumbent — follow-up
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Kumar <anita.kumar@acme-ai.com>, ops@acme-ai.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: End-to-end latency requirements: hosted vs incumbent — follow-up

Anita / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on the product flow and where latency is blocking your user experience. Summarizing the open items and proposing concrete next steps so we can validate fit quickly: 

Open questions we need from your side (action items in bold):
- Confirm end-to-end measurement definition: does your p95/p99 include client-side network and deserialization, or do you want server-to-server model-only numbers? **Please confirm which you prefer for the PoC.**
- Target SLA numbers you want us to validate in the PoC: please confirm p95 and p99 goals for typical payloads (we discussed 256–1024 token outputs).
- Concurrency and traffic profile: peak sustained qps, typical burst shape, and any per-user rate limits.
- Streaming behavior: do you require token-by-token streaming (Server-Sent Events / websockets) or chunked responses are sufficient?

Our immediate plan (proposed):
1) We run a hosted PoC (no infra change on your side) using your sample prompts and our test harness.
2) We measure end-to-end p95/p99 with two profiles: (A) 512-token generation, typical prompt; (B) 128-token generation for short responses.
3) We validate both non-streaming (complete-response) and streaming modes.
4) We compare to your incumbent provider using identical scripts (you can provide an API key for them or we can rely on your supplied logs).

Proposed PoC window: Oct 25–26 (48h window) — please let us know if that works. Deliverables: latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), tail-latency traces, concurrency scaling chart, and a short summary PDF with recommended config changes (batching, kv-cache config, streaming settings).

Attachments: latency-testspec.xlsx (test scripts and payloads), streaming-diagrams.png (how we instrument streaming), SLA-diff-highlights.pdf (what we typically see vs incumbents).

Next steps: 
- Anita: confirm p95/p99 targets + preferred measurement definition by EOD Friday.
- Ops: confirm whether you can provide an API key for the incumbent provider for identical test runs, or we should use your recent operational logs.
- Ben/Laura: we will prepare the hosted PoC plan and test harness.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

---

From: Anita Kumar <anita.kumar@acme-ai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-ai.com, procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: End-to-end latency requirements: hosted vs incumbent — follow-up

Jonas,

Thanks — that plan looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Measurement definition: we want true client-perceived end-to-end numbers (client network + serialization included) because our users see the full wall-clock time. However, for debugging we also want model-only numbers so please capture both.
- Targets (for PoC validation): p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 450ms for 512-token average responses in streaming mode. For short responses (<=128 tokens) we expect p95 < 150ms and p99 < 300ms. These are aggressive but achievable if the serving layer and network are well optimized.
- Concurrency: typical peak is 60 qps for the endpoint we discussed, with short bursts up to 120 qps for ~30s at a time.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming is required for our chat UX; partial-chunk streaming is acceptable if latency per first-byte is within the p95/p99 targets.

We cannot share the incumbent API key but can export the last 72h of production latency logs and a few synthetic traces. I’ve cc'd procurement to start the procurement conversation and ops for the logs.

I can make Oct 25–26 PoC window work; please send exact test times so we can coordinate our traffic shaping.

Regards,
Anita Kumar
Head of Product, AI Services | Acme AI
anita.kumar@acme-ai.com

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Kumar <anita.kumar@acme-ai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: End-to-end latency requirements: hosted vs incumbent — follow-up

Thanks Anita — couple of quick technical clarifications from the infra side so the PoC instrumentation is apples-to-apples: 

1) End-to-end capture: we will run the client driver from your network (if you can provide a short-lived VM/container) to include client network hop; otherwise we’ll simulate the network profile using a shaped egress in our test harness. Which do you prefer?
2) For streaming: are you using websockets or SSE? We can support both; websockets will let us measure first-byte and token-delivery times more precisely.
3) Payload size distribution: please confirm the tokens-per-request histogram for the endpoint (we can use the Excel sheet as a default but would prefer a sample of real prompts).
4) Tracing: we will add x-request-id propagation and provide flamegraphs for any tail requests.

Proposed test schedule (UTC): Oct 25 16:00–20:00 UTC (steady 60 qps + 5x burst tests) and Oct 26 02:00–06:00 UTC (repeat under lower background traffic). We’ll reserve a canary slot the morning of Oct 25 for quick sanity. 

I’ll upload the harness and a small driver container to the shared Drive link; Anita, if you can put ops@acme-ai.com in a temporary allowlist for our test IPs that would speed things up.

- Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Anita Kumar <anita.kumar@acme-ai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-ai.com, procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: End-to-end latency requirements: hosted vs incumbent — follow-up

Ben / Jonas,

Ops just shared a quick summary: our incumbent is averaging p95 ~600ms and p99 ~1.2s on the 512-token profile during peak. That is the source of our user complaints. Procurement is asking for an SLA baseline and a redlines doc — cc'd.

We’ll provide:
- 72h production latency export (attached log_export_72h.csv)
- Sample prompts (sample_prompts.json)

Procurement: can you confirm what you need from Redwood to begin commercial/DocuSign terms? We are evaluating both performance uplift and predictable pricing as decision criteria.

Thanks,
Anita

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Kumar <anita.kumar@acme-ai.com>, ops@acme-ai.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: End-to-end latency requirements: hosted vs incumbent — follow-up

All — thanks for the logs and the clarity on targets. Quick confirmation and final plan before we kick off the PoC: 

1) Measurement: we will report both model-only and client-perceived end-to-end numbers. If you prefer we can run a short test from a container in your VPC for exact client-network effects; otherwise we’ll run with a shaped-network simulation that matches your export.
2) PoC schedule (final): Oct 25 at 15:00 PDT — quick canary + instrumentation check (30m). Oct 25 16:00–20:00 PDT — main steady-state and burst tests. Oct 26 02:00–06:00 PDT — repeat with low background. Team will upload run artifacts to the Drive link above and produce a short summary by Oct 28.
3) Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 450ms for 512-token streaming profile (as requested). If we meet those numbers in our hosted config we will prepare an SLA proposal and an economic analysis (cost per 1k tokens at configured batching/quantization).
4) Deliverables: latency histograms, per-request traces for any > p99 samples, recommended runtime config, and a short executive one-pager for procurement.

Please confirm the canary start time and whether ops wants us to run from a container in your VPC (we can provide a signed short-lived image).

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

(attachments referenced above: latency-testspec.xlsx, streaming-diagrams.png, SLA-diff-highlights.pdf)
